# Mary Vance

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P38](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0038)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  _(assumed)_

## Appearance

Mary Vance initially wore a ragged, faded dress that revealed her scrawny arms and thin hands, which were chapped almost to rawness. She possesses a plump face with rosy cheeks, a pretty mouth with nice, even, white teeth, and unique, queer eyes, alongside hair that is elaborately crimped. She later wears a lovely dress of white embroidered lawn, accented with a scarlet silk sash and shoulder bows.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P27](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0027), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P36](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0036), [v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P5](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028), [v5 CHAPTER XXXIV. UNA VISITS THE HILL P5](../source/v05-c34.md#nw-v05-c34-p0005)_

## Personality

Mary Vance is a brutally frank, lecturing, and slangy girl who can also be seen as silly, though she remains fiercely loyal to her friends. Living in a respectable place, she is motivated by a desire to be a lady and harbours a deep fear of returning to the asylum. Additionally, she is skilled in the kitchen, earning praise as a great cook, and excels at telling blood-curdling ghost stories.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P1](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P7](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0007), [v5 CHAPTER XXIII. ## History

After running away from a traumatic past, the starved waif Mary Vance was found hiding in an old barn by the Meredith children, who fed her at the manse and introduced her to the local youth. She settled into the manse while taking on house chores, but feared being sent to an orphan asylum after Miss Cornelia confronted Mr. Meredith about her background. [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) bravely asked Miss Cornelia to adopt Mary, and after consulting her husband, Miss Cornelia agreed to take the girl into her home. Living with Miss Cornelia, Mary proudly showed off new winter clothes to her friends in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), though she frequently unsettled the other children by relaying local church gossip, telling frightening ghost stories, and sharing horror tales about stepmothers.

_Sources: [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P0](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0000), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P1](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0001), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P2](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0002), [v5 CHAPTER V. THE ADVENT OF MARY VANCE P5](../source/v05-c05.md#nw-v05-c05-p0005), [v5 CHAPTER V. ## Quotes

> "You think you’re something, don’t you, all dressed up like a doll! Look at me. My dress is all rags and I don’t care! I’d rather be ragged than a doll baby. Go home and tell them to put you in a glass case. Look at me—look at me—look at me!"
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER VII. A FISHY EPISODE P9](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0009)

> "If I ever find myself in a place where I ain’t licked I’ll think it’s heaven all right. No fear of me telling lies then. I ain’t fond of telling ‘em—I’d ruther not, if it comes to that."
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P54](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0054)

> "Give me Daniel. I’d rusher have it ‘cause I’m partial to lions. Only I wish they’d et Daniel up. It would have been more exciting."
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P56](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0056)

> "But it won’t be as easy for me to be good—inside, I mean, as well as outside—as it is for you. You hadn’t such scalawags of relations as I had."
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P62](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0062)

> "I never heard of any. My grandfather had money, but they say he was a rascal. No, I’ll just have to start out on my own hook and do the best I can."
>
> — Mary Vance — [v5 CHAPTER IX. UNA INTERVENES P64](../source/v05-c09.md#nw-v05-c09-p0064)

## Relationships

### [Carl](../character/carl.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/carl--mary-vance.md)

Mary Vance met [Carl](../character/carl.md) when his siblings discovered her hiding in a barn, after which she spent time playing with him and the other children in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley). Although she frequently lectures and gossips to the manse children, [Carl](../character/carl.md) considers her a friend, and Mary wept deeply when he later became gravely ill.

- Friend of — cried when he was gravely ill  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XXXI. CARL DOES PENANCE P28](../source/v05-c31.md#nw-v05-c31-p0028)</sub>

### [Di](../character/di.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/di--mary-vance.md)

Mary Vance frequently meets [Di Blythe](../character/di.md) in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), where they gather with the other local children to socialise, read poems, and share ghost stories. Their relationship occasionally sees mild friction, such as when [Di](../character/di.md) steps in to defend [Faith](../character/faith.md) against Mary's sharp criticisms, though they continue to spend tranquil afternoons together.

- Friend of — spending the afternoon together as a treat  <sub>[v5 CHAPTER XVIII. MARY BRINGS EVIL TIDINGS P0](../source/v05-c18.md#nw-v05-c18-p0000)</sub>

### [Faith](../character/faith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/faith--mary-vance.md)

Mary Vance met [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) after runaway Mary was found hiding in an old barn and brought to the manse. ### [Nan Blythe](../character/nan-blythe.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary-vance--nan-blythe.md)

Mary Vance regularly interacts with [Nan Blythe](../character/nan-blythe.md) during group gatherings in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), fascinating and sometimes annoying her with vivid stories and dramatic tall tales. Though [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md) stands up to defend her friends when Mary criticizes their behavior, the two remain friendly companions who enjoy spending afternoons together.

### [Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/mary-vance--una-meredith.md)

[Una Meredith](../character/una-meredith.md) helped shelter Mary Vance when she was a starving runaway, even plucking up the courage to convince Miss Cornelia to adopt Mary to save her from an orphan asylum. [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) acts as a mentor by teaching Mary household tasks like washing dishes nicely, though Mary sometimes causes [Una](../character/una-meredith.md) distress by telling horror stories about potential stepmothers or flaunting new clothes.
